The method and calibration are below; the findings by line follow.

**Method and calibration**
- Backtest predictions were joined to the raw tables by row_id, and I added derived row-structure, cross-line holding and ratio features.
- Probe calibration with random customer labels (40 draws), mean and sd of the gain per year:
  - Contents, 2 levels: mean -0.0001, sd 0.0002.
  - Buildings, 2 levels: similar to contents.
  - Motor uncapped, 2 levels: mean -0.0003 / -0.0016, sd 0.0016. Too noisy to use.
  - Motor with the fitted y capped at 50k: sd 0.0004 / 0.0002.
- Motor full-y D2 is dominated by single claims. The 15.2m row holds 6.6% of 2023 deviance, so motor ideas were judged on capped scores and on a refit as well.

**No information**
- compulsory_excess has a single value within each line.
- Every customer has exactly one motor policy.
- Motor driver_age equals the policyholder's age from date of birth on every row (difference -1/0), so there is no 'driver is not the policyholder' signal.

**Contents** (probe gain 2023 / 2024)
- All 35 unused banded f_* factors were probed; only f_discount passed. - Missing flags: years-at-address missing +0.00008 / +0.00007.
- Row structure: lapse rows, mid-term changes, start and end months all fail or are inconsistent in-sample.

**Buildings**

METHOD NOTES. I wrote two probes in <review scratch>/agents/interactions/: iprobe.py (cells) and pprobe.py, custom.py (parametric). They separate a pure interaction from re-fitted main effects: interaction gain = (main + interaction) minus main only, fitted on one score year and scored on the other.

Two bugs found and fixed along the way:
(a) A fit without an intercept lets the interaction column absorb the year's level, which rebalancing then turns into a distortion (in-sample gains came out negative).
(b) Shrinking band scales towards 1 rather than towards the year's level does the same. The supplied probe.py does (b), which probably explains why a factor already in the model scores about -0.001 there.

This sweep added two data-quality findings, ran six checks that found nothing, and verified several claims the earlier lenses left open.

WHAT THE LENSES COVERED WELL: target development (IBNR, BF, IBNER, recoveries, repudiations, row timing); every unused policy, customer and address field as a banded probe; two-way interactions; GLM and XGBoost structure (power, knots, penalties, tree settings, year weights); level, trend and calibration; claim-history credibility in depth; test-set mix and leaks; and the team's techniques.

WHAT NOBODY EXAMINED, AND WHERE THIS SWEEP FOUND THE TWO GAPS ABOVE: a systematic quality scan of the numeric inputs. Section 2.2's 18 issues were found case by case, and the recode scan covered text fields only. I ran four scans:
- Heaped values in every numeric field: only year_built = 1900 is a placeholder. The other heaps are natural floors or caps (mileage 0 is genuine, with frequency 0.088 against 0.12; days_unoccupied is uniform from 0 to 14).
- Constant-ratio unit errors across more than 30 fields and 12 groupings: only R11 elevation.
- Year drift of numeric fields and categorical shares by year: smooth, apart from the known timber T/W.
- Year-on-year sum insured ratios: only the known x1000 errors plus genuine moves.

Both errors sit in the shared address table, so they also affect the 2025 test rows.

OTHER TABLES AND COLUMNS CHECKED, NOTHING ACTIONABLE:
- Claims are internally consistent: paid never exceeds incurred, closed claims have paid = incurred, nothing is reported before its loss date, and recoveries appear only on closed own-damage and theft claims. Same-day multiple claims are rare (51 motor policy-days) and none repeats an amount.
- repairer_id: 1,000 repairers, each spread over all 12 regions, with no persistent cost (correlation of mean cost across periods 0.03). third_party_id repeats only within the known duplicates.
- surname plus date_of_birth: 9,901 matching pairs against about 9,050 expected by chance, with attributes agreeing at chance rates, so there are no hidden duplicate customers.
- row_id order correlates with the risk mix, but leaves no residual (probe -0.0005).
- Previous-year weather at the address (dryness for subsidence): on fully developed 2022-23 subsidence the lag terms reduce deviance by only 0.5 on 2 degrees of freedom.
- Year-on-year premium change, and premium relative to the prediction: negative on every line.
- R04 and R05 share an identical regional climate. That may be by design, and I did not test its impact.

CLAIMS VERIFIED:
- (a) The interactions lens said probe.py is biased because it shrinks towards 1. A level-corrected probe gives the same figures within 0.0001 (contents f_region -0.00060 / -0.00129 against -0.00066 / -0.00122). The negative scores of factors already in the model are re-estimation noise, so the features-unused scans stand.
- (b) Buildings history E comes from a 12-feature GLM while the XGBoost uses 53 features. Refitting E on 28 or 53 features changes D2 by only -0.00002 to -0.00009, so there is no double counting. Buildings own-line k = 3 gives +0.00006 / +0.00019, which reproduces the customer-history lens.
- (c) C7 (part-year rows): raw rows of exposure 0.1 or less cost 0.17-0.52 of full-year rows in every year 2021-24, with no large claims. The 2022 reversal other lenses found for leaver rows does not extend to these short rows, but the effect rests on 10-22 claims a year.
- (d) customer_service_contacts record the true claims, including unreported ones: about 2.3-2.5 contacts per claim whatever the peril, cost or status. On that basis, the hidden claim counts for 2024 are motor 2,293 +/-177, buildings 559 +/-131 and contents 392 +/-130. These are in line with prior years' late-reported claims: motor 2,162, 2,065 and 1,912+ for 2021-23, matching within the estimator's error. The production n_ibnr_count_basis (motor 1,659) is cost-weighted, so it is not comparable. The check is too imprecise (about +/-8%) to settle #151, but the count side shows no anomaly, which points the motor question at severity and IBNER (C1). Previous-year contacts as a feature show no signal.
- (e) A BF prior adjusted for 2024's dryness (2024 expected subsidence frequency x1.14 against 2022-23 from a clay x dry Poisson model) would raise 2024 subsidence from 11.28m to 11.76m, about +0.7% on the buildings level. That is worth about 0.00001 of D2, so I did not propose it.
